plan.contextChunk: This figure is a ball-and-stick model of one tetraphosphorus trisulfide molecule, P4S3, drawn against a plain white background with no axes or scale. Four orange spheres labeled "P" and three smaller yellow spheres labeled "S" are joined by cylindrical bonds colored in halves, orange on the phosphorus end and yellow on the sulfur end. Three phosphorus atoms form a triangular base across the lower part of the model, drawn in perspective with one sphere at the left, one at the right, and one nearer the viewer at the bottom center; solid orange bonds connect all three directly to one another. A fourth phosphorus sits alone at the apex. Each sulfur bridges that apical phosphorus down to one basal phosphorus, placing the sulfurs at the left, right, and middle of the model, the central one drawn in front with its bond running straight down to the near basal atom. The whole is a closed cage in which every sulfur is two-coordinate and every phosphorus three-coordinate. Splitting each bond into two colors keeps the phosphorus-sulfur links distinct and leaves the three phosphorus-phosphorus bonds around the base unmistakable — direct P-P bonding of the kind that gives phosphorus an oxidation state unusual for a group 15 element.

three direct phosphorus-phosphorus base bonds forming a triangular base: lower-left P to lower-right P, lower-left P to bottom-center foreground P, and lower-right P to bottom-center foreground P

six phosphorus-sulfur bridge bond segments: apical P to left S, left S to lower-left basal P, apical P to right S, right S to lower-right basal P, apical P to central S, and central S to bottom-center foreground P
P-S bonds colored in two halves, orange on the phosphorus end and yellow on the sulfur end
P-P bonds colored solid orange

optional soft specular highlights and mild ambient shadowing to preserve the ball-and-stick textbook style

demo_steps.title: Atom identities
demo_steps.narration: The default view matches the textbook ball-and-stick model: orange atoms are phosphorus and yellow atoms are sulfur. Three phosphorus atoms form the lower triangular base, with the fourth phosphorus at the apex.

demo_steps.narration: Switching to coordination numbers replaces P and S labels with 3 and 2. The overlay makes the cage connectivity explicit: each P has three bonds and each bridging S has two bonds.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Model a single P4S3 cage about 3.6 units wide and 3.5 units tall. Use +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, and +Z toward the viewer. Approximate atom positions: apical P at (0, 1.45, -0.15); lower-left basal P at (-1.45, -0.95, 0.0); lower-right basal P at (1.45, -0.95, 0.0); bottom-center foreground basal P at (0, -1.75, 0.95). Sulfur bridges: left S at (-1.45, 0.35, 0.0); right S at (1.45, 0.35, 0.0); central/front S at (0, -0.05, 0.9). P radius approximately 0.34 world units; S radius approximately 0.32 world units; bond cylinder radius about 0.09. Direct P-P bonds are solid orange cylinders #f58220 connecting lower-left to lower-right, lower-left to bottom-center foreground, and lower-right to bottom-center foreground. P-S bonds are split at their midpoints: orange #f58220 on the P-side and bright yellow #eef22a on the S-side. S spheres should be yellow #e8ee25; P spheres should be orange #f58220 with darker orange shading. Black labels should be bold sans-serif, centered on the camera-facing side of each sphere. In the default camera, the left and right sulfur atoms sit above their basal P atoms, the central sulfur sits in front of the molecule on the vertical line between the apical P and bottom foreground P, and the lower-left to lower-right P-P bond appears nearly horizontal behind the central vertical P-S bridge.
interactionPlan.notes: Use sphere meshes with glossy Phong or standard material and cylinder bonds aligned between atom centers. For P-S bonds, create two separate cylinders per bond so the color changes cleanly at the midpoint. On click, if the user selects any of the three P-P cylinders, highlight all P-P bonds with a brighter orange/emissive outline and dim P-S bonds slightly; if the user selects any half of a P-S bridge, highlight all six P-S half-cylinders while leaving the base triangle subdued. Labels should be implemented as camera-facing sprites or CSS2D text so they remain legible during orbit. In coordination overlay, replace labels rather than adding extra text to avoid clutter.

authoredContext:
The phosphorus distills out of the furnace and is condensed into a solid or burned to form P4O10. The preparation of many other phosphorus compounds begins with P4O10. The acids and phosphates are useful as fertilizers and in the chemical industry. Other uses are in the manufacture of special alloys such as ferrophosphorus and phosphor bronze. Phosphorus is important in making pesticides, matches, and some plastics. Phosphorus is an active nonmetal. In compounds, phosphorus usually occurs in oxidation states of 3−, 3+, and 5+. Phosphorus exhibits oxidation numbers that are unusual for a group 15 element in compounds that contain phosphorus-phosphorus bonds; examples include diphosphorus tetrahydride, H2P-PH2, and tetraphosphorus trisulfide, P4S3, illustrated in the figure.

P4S3 is a component of the heads of strike-anywhere matches.

A ball-and-stick model is shown. Three orange atoms labeled “P” are single bonded together in a triangle shape. Each “P” is single bonded to yellow atoms labeled “S,” which are each single bonded to one other orange atom labeled “P.”
